question: What type of chemical hazard directly destroys living tissue upon contact?
explanation: Corrosive substances such as strong acids and bases cause immediate chemical destruction of skin, mucous membranes, and other tissues upon direct contact. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why are chemical sensitizers particularly challenging in healthcare settings?

options.A: They neutralize all known hospital disinfectants on contact
options.B: They transform into radioactive isotopes inside the human bloodstream
options.C: They instantly ignite when exposed to standard room lighting
options.D: They provoke severe allergic reactions only after repeated previous exposure

explanation: Sensitizers prime the immune system during initial contacts, triggering pronounced and potentially dangerous hypersensitivity reactions during subsequent exposures. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary biological organ responsible for the biotransformation of toxic chemicals?
explanation: The liver contains specialized enzyme systems, notably the cytochrome P450 network, which metabolize foreign chemical compounds and drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why does inhalation of a volatile chemical lead to rapid systemic effects?

options.A: Pulmonary tissues actively pump toxins directly into the central nervous system
options.B: The massive alveolar surface area allows immediate transfer into the pulmonary capillary blood flow
options.C: Inhaled chemicals bypass the liver entirely by exiting through the sweat glands
options.D: The lungs instantly convert all toxic gases into harmless oxygen molecules

explanation: The extremely thin membrane and vast surface area of the lungs facilitate rapid diffusion of gases and vapors straight into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h2)

question: How does cyanide primarily disrupt cellular function?

options.A: By dissolving the structural lipid bilayer of the cell membrane
options.B: By binding to cytochrome c oxidase and halting oxidative phosphorylation
options.C: By directly breaking down DNA strands inside the nucleus
options.D: By precipitating all circulating plasma proteins instantly

explanation: Cyanide targets the electron transport chain in mitochondria, blocking cellular energy production and causing cytotoxic hypoxia. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h3)

question: What differentiates the clinical presentation of acute chemical poisoning from chronic exposure?

options.A: Chronic exposure causes immediate chemical burns, whereas acute exposure has no physical signs
options.B: Acute poisoning is completely asymptomatic for the first five years
options.C: Acute poisoning presents with rapid, dramatic organ failure, whereas chronic exposure causes insidious, long-term organ damage
options.D: Acute poisoning only affects the skin, whereas chronic exposure targets exclusively the brain

explanation: High-dose sudden exposure leads to acute, severe toxicity, while repeated low-dose contact leads to gradual accumulation and chronic systemic illness. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the most effective immediate action for a patient with a corrosive chemical splashed in their eyes?

options.A: Application of an antibiotic ointment to coat the cornea
options.B: Firm patching of both eyes until arrival at a specialist clinic
options.C: Copious irrigation with water or normal saline
options.D: Immediate instillation of neutralizing acid drops

explanation: Immediate, continuous flushing dilutes and washes away the corrosive agent before it can cause permanent structural damage to ocular tissues. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h4)

question: A staff nurse enters a treatment room and finds a colleague collapsed next to an overturned bottle of a volatile organic solvent. What is the priority action?

options.A: Immediately perform mouth-to-mouth resuscitation on the affected colleague
options.B: Run out of the building and call the local police department
options.C: Pour water over the overturned bottle while holding breath
options.D: Ensure personal protective equipment and environmental safety before attempting rescue

explanation: Rescuers must never rush blindly into a chemically contaminated atmosphere without proper protection, otherwise, casualties will multiply. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which pharmacological agent serves as a primary antidote for organophosphate poisoning?
explanation: Atropine blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors, countering the excessive parasympathetic stimulation caused by organophosphates. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h5)

question: How do pharmacological antidotes primarily operate to treat chemical poisoning?

options.A: By coating the gastrointestinal tract to prevent any fluid absorption
options.B: By permanently freezing all metabolic activity within the human body
options.C: By binding toxins, competing for receptors, or accelerating metabolic clearance
options.D: By converting the toxic agent into an inert plastic polymer

explanation: Antidotes counteract poisons through direct chemical inactivation, competitive blocking at target sites, or speeding up the body's natural elimination pathways. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h5)

question: What document must employers make readily accessible to staff detailing chemical hazards and safe handling?
explanation: Safety Data Sheets provide comprehensive technical data regarding chemical properties, hazards, and emergency procedures for safe workplace management. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following practices is NOT permitted when managing workplace chemical agents?

options.A: Transferring chemicals into unlabelled food containers for easy storage
options.B: Consulting Safety Data Sheets prior to cleaning up an unfamiliar spill
options.C: Storing flammable solvents in an approved fire-resistant cabinet
options.D: Wearing heavy-duty chemical-resistant gloves during equipment disinfection

explanation: Using food or beverage containers for chemical storage is a major safety violation that frequently leads to accidental ingestion and severe poisoning. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h6)
